title: Replaying merged changes: how we test whether a knowledge base makes coding agents better

Introduction

Every session, you get a new teammate: a coding agent. It reads code faster than you and has seen more of it than your whole team put together. What it does not have is any memory of how your service got this way.

It can see what the code does. It cannot see why a limit lives in configuration, which nightly job breaks if you touch a shared client, or what an old review thread settled. So it asks, or it guesses.

title: Convert a PDF to Markdown with MinerU from the command line
summary:
You have a PDF report and want it as Markdown: for your notes, or to give to an AI.

How do you do it?

You copy and paste from the PDF viewer. The headings turn into plain lines, and the tables turn into rows of numbers with no columns.

You ask an AI, and it points you to MinerU, which reads the layout and keeps headings and tables. You install it, start its server, and find the command:

mineru parse report.pdf --tier standard --pages 1-10 -o report.md --wait 600

Every flag matters. Leave out --pages and you only get the first 10 pages. Leave out --wait and a long document stops waiting after 60 seconds. --tier trades speed for quality.

title: Credit card interest in code: why a 2% minimum payment takes 110 years at 22.36%
